title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the previous page's statement of the Nakai(–Moishezon)–Mumford ampleness criterion. Setting: X projective over a field k, L invertible. Equivalent conditions:
(a) L is ample.
(b) chi(F⊗L^n) → +∞ for every coherent F with dim Supp F ≥ 1.
(b') The same with F = O_Z, Z integral of dim ≥ 1.
(b'') For every integral Z, some n_Z > 0 has chi(L^n|Z) ≥ 2 if dim Z = 1, and ≥ 1 if dim Z ≥ 2.
(c), (c'), (c'') The same three conditions with chi replaced by h^0.
(d) The crossed-out variants: some L^n has a nonzero section, and deg(L|C) > 0 (or h^0(L^m|C) ≥ 2) for every integral curve C.

This page outlines the proof.
- (a) ⇒ (b),(c): reduce to L very ample and use the Hilbert polynomial.
- (b) ⇒ (b') ⇒ (b'') and (c) ⇒ (c') ⇒ (c''): trivial.
- The converses go by induction on d = dim X. The cases d = 0 and d = 1 are trivial or known; for d = 1 the threshold 2 detects deg > 0, because chi(O_C) ≤ 1 for an integral curve over an algebraically closed field.
- Assume d ≥ 2. By induction the restrictions of L to all proper integral closed subschemes Z are ample.
- Lemma 1: if L|Z is ample for every integral Z of dim < d, then H^i(X, L^n) = 0 for i ≥ 2 and n ≫ 0. The margin notes that only restrictions to divisors are needed, but X must be projective; 'cf. letter to Mumford'. Consequently h^0(L^n) ≥ chi(L^n), which is how the chi-conditions feed into the section conditions (b'') ⇒ (d'').
- (d'') ⇒ (a): reduce to X integral (EGA III). Take a nonzero section f of L^n with zero set D. Since L is not trivial, D ≠ ∅ and dim D = d−1, and L|D is ample by induction.
- Lemma 2: under Lemma 1's hypotheses, if L^n has a nonzero section, then for n ≫ 0 the map X → P(H^0(X, L^n)) is everywhere defined (base-point free) and non-constant. This is the classical Nakai step: from 0 → L^{n−1} → L^n → L^n|D → 0 and the ampleness of L|D, the sections lift.
- Closing questions: (1) in (d), (d'), can the hypothesis that a nonzero section exists be dropped? (2) Can 'X projective' be dropped (i.e. X merely proper)?

The next page applies this to cones of curves and divisors on a surface. There the open question 'x·P > 0 ⇒ x ample?' is reduced via Riemann–Roch and 'Mumford' (h^0 ≥ chi) to the case D^2 = 0, which is exactly where Mumford's counterexample lives.
errors: Over a non-algebraically-closed field the thresholds in (b'') and (c'') are wrong. Take Z = P^1_{k'} for a quadratic extension k'/k, viewed as a k-scheme, with L trivial. Then chi(O_Z) = h^0(O_Z) = 2 ≥ 2, yet L is not ample. One needs k algebraically closed, or thresholds of the form h^0(O_Z)+1.

Gap in (b'') ⇒ (d''). Condition (b'') gives chi(L^n) ≥ 1 for a single n = n_X. Lemma 1 gives h^0(L^n) ≥ chi(L^n) only for n ≥ n_0. As written, (b'') does not yield a nonzero section unless the condition is required for all large n (or for infinitely many n). If L^d > 0 one can of course conclude directly by Nakai.

The first closing question has a negative answer for d ≥ 2: positivity on all curves without a section does not imply ampleness, by Mumford's ruled-surface example with L^2 = 0 (the next page is circling this case). The second has a positive answer: Nakai–Moishezon holds for proper schemes (Kleiman 1966, from memory) and for proper algebraic spaces.
The margin claim 'Mais il faut supposer X projectif' is too pessimistic in light of later work: the standard induction can be carried out for complete schemes.

ideas.what: Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion with an induction on dimension via an effective divisor D in |nL| and vanishing of H^i, i ≥ 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakai (1963), Moishezon (1964); general proper case Kleiman (1966)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA as far as I know; standard expositions are Kleiman 'Toward a numerical theory of ampleness', Hartshorne 'Ample subvarieties'

ideas.what: Reformulation of ampleness via Euler characteristics: chi(F⊗L^n) → ∞ for all coherent F with dim Supp ≥ 1, or chi(O_Z⊗L^n) → ∞ for all integral Z
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert-polynomial form of Nakai's criterion (leading coefficient L^{dim Z}·Z / (dim Z)!)

ideas.what: 'Effective' Nakai variant (c''): L is ample iff deg L|C > 0 for all curves and every integral Z of dim ≥ 2 has some L^n|Z with a nonzero section
ideas.modern_name: Effective-divisor induction step of Nakai's proof, stated as a criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Nakai's proof (Nakai, Kleiman, Hartshorne)

ideas.what: Lemma 1: ampleness on all proper subvarieties implies H^i(X, L^n) = 0 for i ≥ 2 and n ≫ 0
ideas.modern_name: Higher-cohomology vanishing step in the proof of Nakai–Moishezon
ideas.where_published: apparently in a letter to Mumford (referenced on the page)

ideas.what: Lemma 2: an effective L whose restriction to D is ample has L^n base-point free with non-constant map for n ≫ 0
ideas.modern_name: Lifting sections from an ample divisor restriction (Zariski/Nakai argument)

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether positivity on curves plus the existence of a section of some L^n suffices for ampleness in all dimensions (crossed-out d). This is the question of whether effective strictly nef divisors are ample. It is answered positively on surfaces by the L^2 = L·D argument and is related to later work on strictly nef divisors. The question itself is natural and the area is well studied.
missed.quote: Dans l'énoncé d) et d') peut-on supprimer l'hyp. d'existence d'une section ≠ 0 ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Strictly nef versus ample in higher dimensions (e.g. Serrano's conjecture) remains active. It is minor as a historical point: the record shows Grothendieck–Mumford exchanges on this circa 1965.

missed.claim: The page references a 'lettre à Mumford' containing Lemmas 1 and 2 of a Nakai-type proof. This suggests a Grothendieck–Mumford exchange on ampleness criteria (Mumford's counterexample, the cohomological variants) that is not, to my knowledge, in the published correspondence literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Purely historical: it documents how Grothendieck was absorbing Nakai/Mumford in the context of the standard conjectures and cones of cycles (next page).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a sketch of a known theorem (Nakai–Moishezon, plus Mumford's input) with mild cohomological reformulations. The reformulations are natural but implicit in standard proofs. The open questions it raises were answered in the literature: no for (1) by Mumford's example, yes for (2) by Kleiman. Of minor interest are the threshold slip over non-closed fields and the reference to a letter to Mumford.
